rules.title: Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Security deposit may not exceed one and one-half times one month's rent, with annual increases capped at 10% of the current deposit. Deposits must be held in trust in interest-bearing accounts, with interest paid to the tenant annually and written notice of the account given within 30 days.
rules.key_value: 1.5 times monthly rent; annual increase at most 10%; 7% per annum interest if notice/interest not provided
rules.penalty: If proper notice or interest is not provided, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% per annum interest to rent.

exempt_if.name: seasonal_rental
exempt_if.text: seasonal use or rental for a term of not more than 125 consecutive days (interest section only)

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage; the interest section does not apply to seasonal rentals.

rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Termination of a Lease Agreement (lease termination by tenant and landlord limits)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended; a lease may be terminated only where the tenant refuses a new lease with different terms. Tenants may terminate early for specified reasons, such as disability, illness, or domestic violence, with 30 to 40 days' notice.

exempt_if.name: transient_or_seasonal
exempt_if.text: This law does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

coverage.exemptions_summary: Domestic violence termination provisions do not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

rules.quoted_span: The only reason a landlord can terminate a lease is if they offer a new lease to the tenant with different terms, i.e. higher rent or new rules and regulations, and the tenant does not agree. A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.
